items.passage: Mangoes, mostly, though the orchard outside Surabaya had long ago given up deciding. Arisa counted eleven trees still standing and two that had lain down sometime before the rains. Thuy said the fallen ones were resting. Arisa said they were firewood with good manners. They walked the rows the way they had as girls, kicking husks, naming the trees after teachers they had disliked. At the gate Arisa took a parcel from her bag: the brass bell Thuy had mailed to her new flat in Jakarta, still in its paper, the knot untouched. Thuy looked at the knot, not at the bell. She did not ask why. Arisa tied the parcel to the lowest branch of the eleventh tree, where the wind could reach it, and stepped back. They waited. When it rang once, faintly, Thuy reached up and tightened the knot so it would hold through the season.

items.passage: My father kept time by the lamp. “Hand me the blue pins, if you would,” Lakshmi said, and I did, and for an hour we worked the line on the roof of our mother's old boardinghouse in Albuquerque as if no years stood between us. She showed me how to shake a sheet so the wind takes the creases, how to hang shirts by the hem so the shoulders do not pucker, how the adobe parapet holds the morning heat like a palm. She had brought ironed handkerchiefs for me, a dozen, each with my initial stitched in the corner. I thanked her. She asked whether the deed to the house was still kept in the hall desk. I said that it was. We hung the pillowcases. We hung the towels. I thanked her again for the handkerchiefs. That evening I took the deed from the hall desk and carried it to my room, and I folded one of her handkerchiefs around it before I set it beneath my pillow.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text and its significance?
A) It moves from practical lessons to repeated thanks, suggesting the narrator has grown more grateful for her sister's care.
B) It moves from easy fellowship to guarded politeness, suggesting the narrator regrets having said so little about the house.
C) It moves from easy fellowship to guarded politeness, suggesting the narrator suspects the gift served to ease a request.
D) It moves from easy fellowship to guarded politeness, suggesting the narrator has decided to cut off contact with Lakshmi.
### lit40-hard-02-024 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift · 요청 난이도 hard · hard 기준: 전환이 명시되지 않고 겉 어조는 그대로여서 겉 변화만 읽으면 걸리며, 오답이 방향·원인·정도 중 하나만 틀린다
[지문]
What does one say to a brother who has been gone three years? At the depot in Dakar I said nothing useful. I asked Kofi about the ship, and he told me everything: the salt crust on the rails, the cook who sang in Wolof and burned the rice, the porpoises off the cape that the men counted like coins. He laughed often. He asked after our mother, the goats, the mango tree by the well. Then I mentioned that our little brother Chinedu had practiced a salute for him all week. Kofi said that was kind. He said he would like to see it. He picked up his kit bag. On the bus he sat by the window and asked about the price of millet. When we reached the house and Chinedu ran out, standing very straight with his hand at his brow, Kofi knelt, folded the boy's raised hand down into his own, and held it there.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text and its significance?
A) It changes from casual chatter to formal politeness, suggesting Kofi has resumed the manners his family expects at home.
B) It changes from lively storytelling to measured courtesy, suggesting Kofi is ashamed of having talked so long about himself.
C) It changes from lively storytelling to measured courtesy, suggesting Kofi is angry that Chinedu was taught to salute him.
D) It changes from lively storytelling to measured courtesy, suggesting Kofi is uneasy about being honored as a soldier.
### lit40-hard-02-025 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 text_structure · 요청 난이도 hard · hard 기준: 오답이 모두 지문 사실과 일치하고 순서·초점·결말 기능 중 하나만 틀리며, 정답은 재해석 단계를 포함한다
[지문]
Armand had built kites in the yard behind the old silk quarter of Lyon for forty years, and each morning he tested the frames before Okja arrived, bending every spar against his knee and listening for the small dry crack that meant bad wood. Lately he had begun leaving the spars in a heap for her to test alone. Okja took this as impatience. She tested them quickly, tossed the cracked ones aside, and asked for harder work: the great silk dragon for the midsummer festival, the commission he had promised the mayor. Armand said she might begin it. He watched her cut the first panel. That afternoon a carter came for the old drying racks, and Armand counted coins into the man's palm, and the man asked whether the yard would open again in spring. Armand told him to mind the gate. Okja kept cutting silk. When the light failed, he lit the lamp and set it beside her, and went inside without taking his own stool.

[질문] Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
A) It begins with a habit the apprentice misreads, then shows a sale that recasts that habit, and ends with the question left unspoken.
B) It begins with the elder's morning routine, then describes the apprentice's eagerness, and ends with her request for harder work.
C) It begins with a habit that reveals the elder's plans, then shows the apprentice taking it as impatience, and ends with the question unspoken.
D) It begins with a habit the apprentice takes as impatience, then shows a sale that recasts it, and ends with the yard passing to her.
### lit40-hard-02-026 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 text_structure · 요청 난이도 hard · hard 기준: 오답이 모두 지문 사실과 일치하고 순서·초점·결말 기능 중 하나만 틀리며, 정답은 재해석 단계를 포함한다
[지문]
Noa hated weddings. In the hall in Haifa the band played too loud and the aunts pressed honey cake on anyone who sat down, and Yoav, her stepfather, moved through the crowd in a suit slightly too big in the shoulders. __He had worn the same wristwatch every day since she was nine, an old steel one that ran four minutes slow and that he never reset.__ Noa watched him dance with the bride's grandmother, then with a cousin, then with no one, swaying alone near the cake table with his eyes closed. She ate two pieces of honey cake. She checked her phone. At midnight, when the room counted down to the cutting of the cake, Yoav's voice came a little behind everyone else's, as if he were counting by another clock. Afterward he found her by the coat racks, unbuckled the watch, and fastened it on her wrist. Her father's initials were scratched into the back.

[질문] Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
A) It presents a quirk that mainly establishes Yoav as careless about small practical matters.
B) It presents a quirk that later marks the watch as a keepsake of Noa's father.
C) It presents a quirk that explains why Yoav sways alone near the cake table at the wedding.
D) It presents a quirk that illustrates how weddings stir up old habits among the guests.
